subject: Commit transition playbook & proposed ramp schedule (Tiger Data)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@tigerdata.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Commit transition playbook & proposed ramp schedule (Tiger Data)

Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m putting a short playbook and a proposed ramp that smooths your billing quarters while letting you hit the higher committed throughput by Q4. The high-level design:

- Year 1: smaller committed baseline to replace trial/PO usage, with quarterly top-up checkpoints.
- Year 2–3: graduated increases at the start of each fiscal quarter tied to agreed usage triggers.
- Auto-renew: optional 12→24 month auto-extension clause with a performance opt-out window in month 10.
- Co-terming: align all product lines to a single renewal boundary at the end of year 2 to simplify procurement.

I attached the draft TD commit schedule and a one-pager playbook (redwood_transition_playbook.pdf). Can you confirm if procurement needs a specific invoicing cadence or a supplier reference number?

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm invoice cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual prepay).
2) Procurement review and any legal redlines.
3) Finalize penalty/credit language for SLO misses tied to reserved capacity.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30-min call next week to walk through the milestones.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: td_commit_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)
Attachment: redwood_transition_playbook.pdf (pdf, 180KB)

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@tigerdata.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@tigerdata.com>, Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@tigerdata.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Commit transition playbook & proposed ramp schedule (Tiger Data)

Diego —

Appreciate the clear outline. A few quick clarifications from our side before we loop legal:

- Invoicing: prefer quarterly invoicing with a monthly usage true-up. Is Redwood able to provide token-level cost reconciliation for the true-up?
- Opt-out window: can you summarize what "performance opt-out" looks like for us (notice period, metrics)?
- Co-terming impact: if we align to year 2, how do you handle partial-period credits for products that start mid-year?

Cc'ing procurement and Samantha (Finance) so they can flag any internal constraints. If you can reply with bullets, we’ll triage internal approval quickly.

—Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, Tiger Data
alex.kim@tigerdata.com | (212) 555-0199

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@tigerdata.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Kim Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Commit transition playbook & proposed ramp schedule (Tiger Data)

Alex — quick answers below; I also added Kim to call out commercial specifics. More detail in the attached schedule.

- Quarterly invoicing + monthly true-up: yes, we can provide token-level reconciliation exports (CSV) for the true-up window. We’ll include a sample export format in the final contract appendix.
- Performance opt-out: defined SLOs are availability and median p99 latency for your primary 8k token workloads. Opt-out requires a 60-day notice and must be based on sustained SLO misses across two consecutive quarters; if triggered, you get an escape right to revert to month-to-month for a 90-day remediation period or a pro‑rated credit for the affected quarter.
- Partial-period credits for co-terming: we offer pro-rata credits for any product that’s moved into the new co-term period; credits are applied to the following invoice cycle. For major mid-year migrations we can create an escrowed credit to smooth billing spikes.

Proposed ramp (excerpt from td_commit_schedule.xlsx):
- Q2 2026: baseline commit = 12M tokens/month (replace trial usage).
- Q3 2026: increase to 20M tokens/month if 75% utilization on baseline in two consecutive months.
- Q4 2026: increase to 35M tokens/month contingent on agreed benchmark results and a business KPI check-in.

I’ll set up a short walkthrough (30m) with you and procurement. Kim — feel free to add any pricing notes.

—Diego

Attachment: td_commit_schedule.xlsx (updated version)

From: Kim Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@tigerdata.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Pricing sketch & DocuSign cadence for the Tiger Data transition

Alex / team —

Thanks for the prompt follow-up. Attached is a lightweight pricing sketch with two options: (A) graduated discount ladder tied to utilization thresholds; (B) flat blended rate with an annual true-up. Highlights:

- Option A (recommended): 5% discount at 60% baseline utilization; 12% at 80%; 18% at 95% — applies to committed token pricing.
- Option B: single blended unit price for simplicity; true-up annually with pro-rata credits for early scale.

For contracting cadence, we typically:
1) Share redline-friendly contract PDF + HubSpot deal record (link above).
2) Procurement reviews and requests changes (we handle minor invoicing/legal revisions).
3) Send final via DocuSign for signature; preferred signatory cadence is single-signer on your end to avoid routing delays.

I’ve attached pricing_sketch.csv and can prep a DocuSign envelope as soon as we lock the option. Marissa — wanted to loop you for the SLO credit band thresholds we discussed.

Thanks,
—Kim
Kimberly Park
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing_sketch.csv (csv, 6KB)

If procurement is green, we’ll accept the DocuSign envelope flow. Diego/Kim — please send the final contract with the SLO credit bands and the sample token reconciliation CSV and we’ll route it for signature next week.

Action items agreed:
